shared_elements: low-relief carving on a tall pale stone slab
quadruped or crouching beast at lower left
band or block of repeated small geometric units (net/zigzag band in A, grid of squares in B)
curved arc/hoop motifs near the top
justification: Both are tall, pale stone slabs worked in shallow relief with profile creatures and a bounded field of repeated small geometric units (A's zigzag/net band, B's grid of squares), and each places a crouching animal-headed form at the lower left. But A distributes a few isolated, sparse silhouettes across horizontal registers with much blank ground, whereas B is a single dense, horror-vacui composition dominated by one elaborately costumed standing figure, so the manner of carving and the compositional logic differ fundamentally.
